summary: This work demonstrates erasure conversion in a single fluxonium qubit operated at zero flux, where the logical qubit is encoded in the $|0\rangle$–$|2\rangle$ subspace and physical relaxation is routed through the intermediate $|1\rangle$ state as a detectable erasure. A single resonator coupled dispersively to the qubit performs both mid-circuit erasure detection and end-of-line logical readout, achieving a four-fold increase in logical lifetime from 193 µs to 869 µs via post-selection on non-erasure outcomes.
motivation: Dual-rail erasure qubits in cavities and transmons require substantial hardware overhead and circuit complexity. This work seeks a hardware-efficient single-qubit platform for erasure-based error mitigation by exploiting symmetry-induced suppression of direct decay at zero flux.
method: An integer fluxonium with $E_c/\hbar = 2\pi \times 1.72$ GHz, $E_J/\hbar = 2\pi \times 7.07$ GHz, and $E_L/\hbar = 2\pi \times 0.32$ GHz is operated at $\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}} = 0$ to suppress the charge matrix element $|\langle 0|\hat{n}|2\rangle|$, forcing decay through $|1\rangle$. A single resonator with tunable dispersive shifts ($\chi_{02} = -2\pi \times 147$ kHz at $\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}} = 0$, $\chi_{02} = -2\pi \times 760$ kHz at $\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}} = 1.3$ m$\Phi_0$) enables selective erasure detection without perturbing the computational manifold.
result: At $\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}} = 0$, the direct transition rate $\Gamma_{20}$ is suppressed to below the measurement threshold while $\Gamma_{10} = 2\pi \times 1.22$ kHz and $\Gamma_{21} = 2\pi \times 1.21$ kHz remain comparable. Post-selection on erasure-free runs increases $T_{1L}$ from 193 µs to 869 µs, while each erasure check contributes a negligible pure-dephasing error of $7.2 \times 10^{-5}$ and QND infidelity below 0.1 % per check.
